findings.claim: The client-secret scan still allows common service-role environment variables such as `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` in example `.env` files.
findings.evidence: The acceptance criterion says "Client examples never expose service-role credentials," and the new scan now includes `.env*` files, but the forbidden patterns only check `FLINT_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, `service_role_...`, `flint_sk_...`, and `VITE_...SECRET|PRIVATE|SERVICE`; a non-VITE `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=...` or generic `SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=...` in `examples/**/.env` is not matched.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject generic service-role variable names in scanned text, e.g. `/\b(?:SUPABASE_)?SERVICE_ROLE(?:_KEY)?\b/i`, and add a regression with `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` in an example env file.

findings.claim: The machine-specific path verifier still misses Windows absolute Flint sibling roots outside `C:\Users`.
findings.evidence: The acceptance/evidence constraint requires rejecting machine-specific absolute Flint paths, but `findMachineSpecificPath` only matches Windows paths under `[A-Za-z]:\\Users\\...` and the `absoluteFlintRoot` regex only matches Unix-style `/.../flint-realtime-fabric|flint-gate|flint-forge`; paths like `D:\checkouts\flint-gate\src\index.ts` evade the check.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Windows drive-root Flint path pattern such as `/[A-Za-z]:\\(?:[^\\\s"'`]+\\)*?(?:flint-realtime-fabric|flint-gate|flint-forge)(?:\\|$)/i` and cover it in the path regression test.
